info.title: Linkwise API
info.summary: Save, search, organise and read the things you collect.
info.description:
The public HTTP API for Linkwise, served by the `api` edge function.

This document is the source of truth. The MCP server's tool definitions and
the CLI's commands are generated from it, so neither can drift from what the
API actually serves. Change the API here first.

See `README.md` in this directory for auth, pagination and error handling
prose, and `inventory.md` for the other 83 edge functions that sit behind
this one.

get.description: The only unauthenticated endpoint, so uptime checks need no credential.

Newest first by default. All filters combine with AND.

Note the tri-state booleans: omitting `archived` is not the same as
`archived=false`. Omitted means no filter on that column.

parameters.name: archived
parameters.description: Defaults to false, i.e. archived links are hidden.

parameters.name: no_collection
parameters.description: Only links not filed in any collection.

parameters.name: is_email
parameters.description: Only links that arrived by email drop.

post.description:
Returns immediately. Fetching, parsing, chunking and embedding happen
asynchronously, so `processing_status` will be pending on the response
and the reader content and transcript endpoints will 404 until it
completes.

**Idempotent, on a best-effort basis.** Saving a URL already in your
library returns `200` with the existing link and `meta.already_existed`
true, rather than creating a duplicate. It is best-effort because the
canonical URL is only known after the link is fetched and redirects are
followed, so a link submitted twice in quick succession, or submitted
under two URLs that redirect to the same place, can still produce two
rows. Check the status code to tell the cases apart: `201` created,
`200` already there.

Plan limits are enforced with the same `check_user_limits` RPC the apps
use, so this cannot be used to exceed a quota the UI honours. The limit
is only consulted when a link is actually created.

title.description: Overrides the title parsed from the page.

description.description: Your own summary. Kept: process_link only fills description when the link has none, so supplying one here is not overwritten when the page is parsed.

tags.description: Tag names. Any that do not exist are created.

200.description:
This URL was already in the library. The existing link is returned
and nothing was created.

201.description: Link saved and queued for processing

patch.description:
Only the fields present in the body are changed.

`is_pinned` is applied through the pin RPC rather than written directly,
because the number of pins allowed depends on the plan. Sending it
toggles the pin rather than setting it to the value supplied.

description.description: Your own summary. Send null to clear it.

archived.description: True sets archived_at to now; false clears it.

is_pinned.description: Toggles the pin. Subject to the per-plan pin cap.

delete.description:
A soft delete, matching the apps: the row is marked deleted and stops
appearing, and is purged later by the archive lifecycle job.

get.description:
The parsed, sanitised article body, plus a computed outline. 404s while
the link is still processing, or when the page yielded no readable
article.
For YouTube and other media links. 404s when there is none.

get.summary: Get AI insights for a link
get.description:
Read-only. Generating an insight is metered and asynchronous; that
endpoint is not in v1 yet. 404s when none has been generated.

put.description:
Replaces the whole set rather than adding to it. Send the complete list
you want; an empty array removes them all. Tags that do not exist yet
are created.

get.description: Returns every collection with its link count. Not paged.

is_public.description: Publishes the collection at a shareable URL.

is_pinned.description: Toggles the pin. Subject to the per-plan cap.

delete.description: Soft delete. Links inside it are not deleted, only unfiled.

200.description: A page of tags with link counts

post.description: Idempotent. Creating a tag that already exists returns the existing one.

delete.description: Soft delete. The tag is removed from every link that had it.

post.description:
Offsets are character positions into the reader content, so a highlight
created against one parse may not line up if the article is re-parsed.

article_url.description: Defaults to the link's own URL.

404.description: The link does not exist or is not yours

patch.description: Only the colour and annotation can change. Offsets and text are immutable.

delete.description: A hard delete. Highlights have no soft-delete column.

get.description:
`hybrid` is the ranked path the apps use and is the default. `fast` is
trigram and full-text only: cheaper and lower latency, but it will not
find a document that never uses the query's words.

Semantic-only search is deliberately absent. It needs a query embedding,
which costs credits, so it sits behind chat instead.
Full-text over highlighted passages and their annotations.

Personalised, ranked against a taste vector built from what you save and
like.

The ordering is seeded. Omit `seed` and one is generated for you and
returned in `meta.seed`; the returned `next_cursor` carries it. Pass the
same seed to keep paging through one stable ordering. Change it to
reshuffle.

post.description:
Trains the recommendation model. Recording any interaction also marks
the item as seen, so it stops being served again.

dwell_ms.description: Milliseconds spent on the item. Meaningful with `dwell`.

post.summary: Save a discovery item to the library

post.description:
Send `url` to discover a feed from a site address, handle or feed URL.
Discovery tries the platform-specific path first (Substack, Medium,
Ghost, WordPress), then `<link rel=alternate>`, then common paths.

Send `feed_id` instead to subscribe to a feed already known to Linkwise,
which skips discovery entirely.

400.description: No feed could be found at that address

delete.description: Removes your subscription. The feed itself is shared and is not deleted.

get.description: Standard OPML 2.0, importable by any other reader.

post.description:
Streams Server-Sent Events.

`library` scope requires Pro. `link` and `collection` scopes require
`context_id`.

**Not yet available with a personal access token.** The upstream chat
functions resolve their user from a session JWT and there is nothing to
forward for a PAT, so a PAT gets an explicit error rather than being
silently run as the wrong user.

conversation_id.description: Omit to start a new conversation.

200.description: An SSE stream of tokens and tool events

500.description: Not available with a personal access token

post.description:
Requires Pro, and charges credits. Returns a URL to cached audio plus
speech marks for word-level highlighting.

**Not yet available with a personal access token**, for the same reason
as `/v1/chat`.

get.description:
Identity, plan and how this request authenticated. Deliberately narrow:
it does not return deletion tokens, suspension state or onboarding
internals.

patch.description: Username uniqueness and format are validated server-side.

get.description: Ask whether an action is currently allowed, before attempting it.

200.description: Whether the action is allowed, and the relevant quota

get.description:
Session JWT only. Never returns token values, only their display
prefixes.

403.description: Called with a personal access token

post.description:
Session JWT only. A token cannot mint another token.

**The plaintext value is returned once, here, and never again.** Only a
SHA-256 hash and a display prefix are stored.

Maximum ten active tokens per account.

expires_in_days.description: Omit for a token that never expires.

201.description: Created. `token` appears only in this response.

token.description: The plaintext token. Store it now.

delete.description: Session JWT only. Takes effect immediately.

personalAccessToken.description:
A Linkwise personal access token, `lw_pat_` followed by 32 random bytes.
Create one at `POST /v1/tokens` with a signed-in session. Scope-limited.

sessionJwt.description:
A Supabase session JWT. Holds every scope, matching what the same token
can already do against PostgREST directly. Required for `/v1/tokens`.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description:
From a previous response's `meta.next_cursor`. Opaque: do not construct
or parse one. Takes precedence over `limit`.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, revoked or expired credential

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but this token lacks the required scope

NotFound.description:
No such resource. Also returned when a resource exists but belongs to
someone else, so ids cannot be probed for existence.

ProRequired.description: The feature requires a Pro subscription

message.description: Human-readable. Do not branch on this; branch on `code`.

ErrorCode.description:
A closed set. HTTP status is derived from this in one place, and message
text never affects it.

next_cursor.description: Null when this is the last page.

total.description: Present only when the underlying query reports one.

normalized_url.description: Canonical form used for deduplication. Tracking parameters removed.

description.description: Editable through PATCH. Parsed from the page when a link is saved without one, and never overwritten by parsing afterwards.

processing_status.description: Pending until fetching, parsing and embedding finish.

broken_at.description: Set when a link check found the URL unreachable.

html_content.description: Sanitised. Scripts, event handlers and javascript URLs removed.

outline.description:
Table of contents computed server-side from the same HTML. Ids match
the anchors the reader injects, so an entry can be scrolled to.

is_locked.description: True when the collection is beyond the plan's link allowance.

name_slug.description: Frozen at creation. Used in the public share URL.

snippet.description: Matching passage, with the query terms in context.

token_prefix.description: First 11 characters, for display. Not a usable credential.
